variant: Hyryder V Aero Black Edition AWD AT
pros: Light on the wallet: The strong hybrid petrol powertrain offers segment-best fuel efficiency
Capable drivetrain: For the adventure enthusiasts, it comes with the option of an AWD powertrain
Plush & Spacious cabin: Comes with good quality plastics and soft touch materials along with good space for 4 people
Feature loaded: panoramic sunroof, 360-degree camera, ventilated front seats and digital driver’s display
Appealing design: Looks classy and sophisticated, which will appeal to a lot of buyers
cons: Not exciting: The performance feels just about adequate and you won’t get a very fun to drive experience
Not for tall people: While there is good space in the back, the rear seat headroom is just average for tall passengers, especially in the panoramic sunroof variants
Less powertrain options: While there is strong-hybrid and a mild-hybrid petrol options, there is no diesel engine on offer
Limited boot space: Due to the large battery pack in the strong hybrid variants, boot spaces gets restricted

pros: Cabin: Good space and practicality for 4 adults
Styling that'll age well. New elements like the illuminated logos make it stand out more.
Boot space: Not the biggest on-paper, but very practical for daily use
Performance: Both 1-litre and 1.5-litre turbo-petrol engines offer good performance
Driving dynamics: Feels fun to drive without any big compromise in ride comfort
cons: No ADAS features could be a miss for people who do long intercity trips
Rear-view camera: Poor resolution limits usability. No 360-degree camera option
Powertrain options: No CNG, diesel or hybrid powertrain options

pros: Loaded with features: 15-inch touchscreen, 11 speaker Harman Kardon audio, massage seats etc.
Classy styling. Looks rich and premium without being shouty.
Strong performance. 0-100kmph in 7.3 seconds and 224kmph top speed make it a driver’s SUV.
Premium interior experience with soft-touch leatherette and alcantara trims.
cons: Not a true seven-seater. Getting in/out of the third row is tough, space inadequate for adults
No diesel or hybrid options.

pros: Powerful turbo-petrol engine: Offers an engaging drive experience and suspension set up gives you the best of both words - comfortable and sporty when you want it to be.
Spacious and practical: Offers plenty of room, lots of cubby holes and charging options. Dual wireless charging up front is a great feature.
Impressive tech package: Comes with a 15-inch touchscreen, a digital driver's display, and a HUD too
Great seats: R-Line seats give you a good driving position and are comfortable and supportive. Massage function is good.
cons: Missing features: Does not get keyless entry, powered and ventilated front seats
Not so efficient: Fuel efficiency of the large turbo-petrol engine in traffic and when driven with a heavy right foot can drop

pros: Sophisticated look: Classy, understated styling. Sporty GT variant on offer too
Strong engine options: 1- and 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engines promise excitement
Great boot space: 521 litre boot is segment leading. 60:40 split rear seats bumps up practicality
Feature-loaded: 8-inch digital driver’s display, 10.1-inch touchscreen, ventilated seats, electric sunroof are among the highlights
cons: Limited powertrains: No diesel of hybrid engine options. City offers a strong hybrid powertrain.
Less rear seat space: Lack of width and strong seat contouring means the Virtus is best used as a four seater
